newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-West power steady under cold conditions.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-West power steady under cold conditions.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady Monday with few utilities offering peak power, choosing instead to hold on to capacity ahead of cold temperatures Tuesday, sources said.
"People are holding off on selling, tomorrow is probably going to be the coldest day of the winter," said one Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) trader.

Temperatures in northern reaches of the Mid-West were expected to be 10 to 15 degrees below normal through to at least Wednesday, with overnight lows in North Dakota reaching below zero degrees Fahrenheit.

In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm next day power deals were pegged steady at $27.50-29.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) with little spot business reported done other than some expensive hourly power trades.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were also said to be scarce, but were notionally pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the brokers and marketers said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Tuesday delivery was pegged steady at $25.00-27.00, again with few 16-hour deals being done.
Weekend peak MAIN power was assessed at $15.50-17.50 per MWh, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday delivery were assessed at $27.00-28.00 from $27.00-29.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
December peak ECAR was talked steady at $22.00-23.00, with January/February ECAR also assessed steady at $23.00-24.00 per MWh.
Peak non-firm power prices in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP) for the weekend and Monday were talked steady at $25.00-27.50, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area.
December SPP was assessed lower at $25.00-27.00 from $26.50-27.50 late last week, while January/February was pegged near $27.00 per MWh, the brokers and marketers said.
